scope: C-24/C-29 frame interpretation and C-17 noise conditions under H-74/H-75/H-78

frame_semantics.direct_map: For x[k+1]=W*x[k], fixed W advances one graph transition per frame. Halving Delta makes two graph transitions in the former physical interval, giving W^2 rather than W.
frame_semantics.no_generic_half_step: For the two-coordinate swap P=[[0,1],[1,0]], no real 2x2 matrix V satisfies V^2=P because det(V)^2>=0 while det(P)=-1. A direct frame map need not have a same-state continuous-time refinement. This is a linear algebra counterexample, not a demand to add state.
frame_semantics.local_leak_limit: A coefficient 1-exp(-Delta/tau) makes a frozen-drive scalar relaxation step-consistent; it does not make the complete nonlinear recurrent transition exact or preserve all path delays.
frame_semantics.half_life: For fixed ring gains and L stages, H=-L*Delta*log(2)/log(G). Recalibrating G can preserve this envelope scale but does not by itself preserve lap or entry timing.
frame_semantics.decision_boundary: A fixed discrete modeling interval is a valid candidate. A finer interval is not automatically more accurate until an underlying time law and comparison meaning are specified; no Delta, continuous model, delay array or scheduler is selected.

noise_arithmetic.assumptions: Scalar additive recurrence without leak, for physical duration T with T/Delta whole steps; independent zero-mean unit-variance zeta. This reference is not the positive-rate input law of the application.
noise_arithmetic.meaning: The three laws have different units and model meanings. Temporal whiteness alone does not select one or specify spatial correlation, positive kicks versus signed drive, distribution or controller update time.
noise_arithmetic.source: Higham2001 sections2 and4: Brownian increments have variance Delta, and enter Euler-Maruyama separately from Delta-scaled drift; this does not select Brownian noise or an SDE for the SNN.

comparison_conditions: Compare physical token duration, response half-life, regulation cadence and coverage windows in model time, not unchanged frame counts.

For a selected continuous stochastic reference, pathwise refinement must aggregate the same increments over coarse intervals; independent new paths confound pathwise error. Distributional behavioral comparisons have a different purpose.
Nonlinear thresholds and cancellation can distinguish noise distributions even when their first two moments agree. No sampling implementation or generic experiment framework is selected.

noise_averaging_reference.assumptions: Static binary threshold at theta, Gaussian input variability with standard deviation sigma>0; f_sigma(mu) is its expected output after this variability has already been averaged. Additional explicit independent Gaussian variability has standard deviation tau. This is not a spiking or recurrent simulation, and no Gaussian noise law is selected for the application.
noise_averaging_reference.response: f_sigma(mu)=Phi((mu-theta)/sigma), with Phi the standard normal CDF.
noise_averaging_reference.derivation: The conditional probability becomes Pr(sigma*Z1-tau*Z2 <= mu-theta); independent centered Gaussian variances add. Averaging twice over independent replicas of one intended noise source instead changes the total variance.

verification.method: Independent composite Simpson quadrature over Z in[-10,10],8192 subintervals for each of12 cases. Bounded CDF integrand leaves less than1.6e-23 Gaussian tail mass outside that range. Agreement is an arithmetic check, not a bound on application error.

noise_averaging_reference.interpretation: An averaged transfer curve and explicit variability can coexist when they represent different intended sources or resolutions. Treating the same background variability in both places changes the reference model. A phenomenological transfer is not automatically noise-averaged.
noise_averaging_reference.limits: One-step mean response only: no temporal kernel, cancellation, adaptive regulator, individual path retention, neuronal thresholds or physical time selected.
noise_averaging_reference.primary_context: MR-S087 explains trial-averaged firing-rate reduction and noise-dependent transfer/filter properties. This Gaussian threshold identity is independently derived, not that paper's neuron equation.

cancellation_and_ensemble_mean.assumptions: One candidate cell in each polarity of a minicolumn independently receives0 or1 with probability p of1; other cells are zero. Apply H77 minicolumn-wide net cancellation once. This special case does not introduce paired-cell cancellation, a noise law or binary runtime states.
cancellation_and_ensemble_mean.identity: E[C(P,M)]=(p*(1-p),p*(1-p)), whereas C(E[P],E[M])=(0,0). Both signed means are zero; unsigned response and realized participation differ.
cancellation_and_ensemble_mean.verification: Enumerated all4 outcomes with exact Fraction probabilities for3 p values; no random draws or neural trajectories.
cancellation_and_ensemble_mean.interpretation: An ensemble/time-averaged post-cancellation value can contain both polarities although every individual completed frame obeys H77. It is not itself an admissible instantaneous post-cancellation snapshot with that same interpretation. A deterministic effective-rate model remains possible, but equating its trajectory to averaged stochastic trajectories requires additional justification.
cancellation_and_ensemble_mean.non_adoptions: No second moment, distribution state, spike simulator, new cancellation policy or selection of deterministic versus stochastic rates. Existing individual contextual identities and two-frame publication remain.

positive_kick_scaling.assumptions: Scalar sum over T/Delta independent positive U[0,A_Delta] kicks; no leak, transfer, cancellation, recurrence or feedback. T/Delta is integer. This is not a neuron simulation or selected noise law.

amplitude_only_scaling.A_equals_cDelta: Mean=c*T/2; variance=c^2*T*Delta/12 tends to0 as Delta shrinks.
amplitude_only_scaling.A_equals_csqrtDelta: Variance=c^2*T/12; mean=c*T/(2*sqrt(Delta)) grows without bound as Delta shrinks.
amplitude_only_scaling.conclusion: For this fixed-shape nonnegative-kick family, amplitude rescaling alone cannot preserve both positive mean input and nonzero accumulated variance under arbitrary frame refinement.

limits: This does not prohibit positive-noise models or require a continuous-time limit. A fixed discrete model interval remains valid.
Centered temporal whiteness is compatible with a nonzero mean; zero-mean Brownian scaling cannot silently be applied to the uncentered positive kicks.
Other distributions, event probabilities or noise inside a nonlinear rate response have different limits and require their own declared units.
No offset, event process, sampler, noise channel, new state or controller is chosen.
positive_kick_scaling.verification: Eight exact rational moment cases; no random draws or neural evolution generated.
